title: Constants: const and #define
instructions: A constant is a value that must never change. Two ways to make one:
- const int MAX = 100; makes a variable you promise not to change. If you try, the compiler stops you.
- #define PI 3.14 (at the top, no semicolon) makes a name that stands for a fixed value everywhere.
Constants make code safer and clearer: PI reads better than 3.14 scattered around, and const stops accidental changes.
By tradition, constant names are written in CAPITALS.
task: Add a const int named MAX set to 100, so the output ends with:  MAX = 100
hint:
Declare it with const:

    const int MAX = 100;
